walkthrough.auth:checking: First, I'm making sure you're signed in to WorkOS.
walkthrough.auth:failure: I couldn't confirm your WorkOS sign-in.
walkthrough.scaffold:prompt: This folder is empty, so I can create a new Next.js app here for you.
walkthrough.scaffold:start: Creating a new Next.js app with {packageManager}. This can take a minute.
walkthrough.detection:start: Now I'm looking around your project to see what it's built with.
walkthrough.detection:complete: This is a {framework} app. I know how to set that up.
walkthrough.detection:none: I couldn't tell which framework this project uses.
walkthrough.git:dirty: You have uncommitted changes (files: {count}), so I'll check with you before going further.
walkthrough.git:dirty:confirmed: Okay, carrying on. I'll leave your existing changes alone.
walkthrough.branch:protected: You're on {branch}. I'll ask whether to put these changes on their own branch.
walkthrough.branch:created: I made a new branch, {branch}, so these changes stay separate.
walkthrough.credentials:gathering: Next, I need the WorkOS keys for your app.
walkthrough.credentials:found: I'll use the WorkOS keys you already have.
walkthrough.device:started: Open {url} in your browser and enter the code {code} to connect this computer to WorkOS.
walkthrough.credentials:request: Paste your WorkOS keys below. You'll find them at dashboard.workos.com.
walkthrough.config:start: Setting up WorkOS for this app: redirect URIs, sign-in settings, and environment variables.
walkthrough.agent:start: Now the AuthKit agent is adding sign-in to your code. This usually takes a few minutes, so it's a good time for a coffee.
walkthrough.agent:failure: The agent ran into a problem.

validation:complete.failed: A few things are worth a look (issues: {count}). They'll be listed when this screen closes.

walkthrough.postinstall:manual: The GitHub CLI isn't installed, so here's how to open the pull request yourself.

complete.failure: The install didn't finish. The details will be shown when this screen closes.

tips.title: Add Enterprise SSO
tips.body: Let your customers sign in with Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, and more.

tips.title: Let IT admins set up SSO themselves
tips.body: Send a customer's IT team a link to the Admin Portal instead of a setup call.

tips.title: Sync users from your customers' directories
tips.body: Directory Sync keeps users and groups up to date from Okta, Entra ID, and Google.

tips.title: Group users into organizations
tips.body: Organizations are how WorkOS models your customers. Create one right from your terminal.

tips.title: Add roles and permissions
tips.body: Define roles once and check them in your app with role-based access control.

tips.title: Make AuthKit look like your app
tips.body: Set your logo and colors so the sign-in page feels like home.

tips.title: Turn on passkeys
tips.body: Let users sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, or a security key.

tips.title: Keep an audit trail
tips.body: Record who did what, and let your customers export it for their compliance teams.

tips.title: Teach your coding agent WorkOS
tips.body: Install WorkOS skills so your coding agent knows the APIs and best practices.

tips.title: Something not working?
tips.body: The doctor checks your AuthKit setup and explains what to fix.

tips.title: AuthKit for Next.js
tips.body: See how to protect routes and read the signed-in user in your Next.js app.

tips.title: AuthKit for React
tips.body: See how to read the signed-in user and protect parts of your React app.

announcements.title: See what's new at WorkOS
announcements.body: New features and improvements ship every week.

announcements.title: Run your whole WorkOS account from the CLI
announcements.body: Manage organizations, users, roles, webhooks, and more without leaving your terminal.
